preamble: Total regressive assimilation of /l/ to a following uvular /q/ is attested in a single but well-known Hebrew verb: in לָקַח lāqaḥ 'take' the lamed behaves like the nun of I-nun verbs and assimilates to the following qof, giving the imperfect יִקַּח yiqqaḥ with a geminate qq. It is a lexically restricted, sporadic assimilation rather than a regular sound change.

examples.note: The lamed of לָקַח is treated like the nun of I-nun verbs and assimilates totally to the following qof, leaving a doubled qq (Gesenius §66g). The same root otherwise keeps its l (perfect לָקַח lāqaḥ).

sources: Gesenius, W., Kautzsch, E., & Cowley, A. E. (1910). Gesenius' Hebrew Grammar, §66 Verba Primae Radicalis Nûn. https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Gesenius%27_Hebrew_Grammar/66
